title: Attack-Inference Aligned Universal Adversarial Attacks on Video Object Segmentation
claim: Attacks aligned with the two-stage inference pipeline stay effective across all prompt types and persist over time, unlike prior attacks.
layout: 2 panels: pipeline diagram left, two stacked prior-vs-ours comparisons right
description: The left panel, titled Training-time Optimization, shows a timeline from Initialization at t=1 to Propagation at t=2 through t=n. Each time step is a column with a video frame of a bus, a blue VOS model bar, black predicted mask frames, a green memory encoder bar and a grey memory bank at the bottom. Crossed-sword icons and heatmap perturbations mark where the attack enters the model. Orange arrows run from the memory bank back to the VOS model. The first frame shows four prompt icons: mask, point, box and language. A dotted divider separates this from the right panel, Inference-time comparison. The right panel has two rounded boxes. Prompt-agnosticism compares Prior and Ours across Mask, Point, Box and Language, using red crosses and green checks. Temporal persistency shows mask sequences. Prior recovers a pink bus mask over time, while Ours stays black, meaning the attack holds.
caption: \methodname aligns attack optimization with the two-stage VOS inference pipeline (initialization and propagation), yielding more persistent and prompt-agnostic attacks than prior methods.
abstract: Modern video object segmentation (VOS) relies on a two-stage inference paradigm: target initialization and memory-based propagation. However, existing adversarial attacks on VOS often overlook this structure. To bridge this gap, we propose AUV, an adversarial framework that Aligns with the Universal two-stage paradigm of VOS models. Specifically, AUV optimizes a universal adversarial perturbation (UAP) through decoupled training strategies tailored for both initialization and propagation stages. By disrupting the shared memory space, it achieves prompt-agnostic attacks across different modalities, including masks, points, boxes, and language. Extensive experiments show that AUV establishes state-of-the-art VOS attack performance, such as degrading mask-based SAM3 to only 8.4 J&F on DAVIS17-val (compared to 55.4 for the previous SOTA under the same training setup). It also exhibits superior temporal dynamics with the fastest onset, the most enduring persistence, and the support of any-time mid-video attacks. The AUV optimization framework is applicable to different VOS models, revealing vulnerabilities in real-world streaming VOS. Code is available at https://github.com/FudanCVL/AUV.
